summary: Replace the uniform grid with the known optimal "one large rotated/axis-aligned square plus a strip of small squares" style packing: for non-square n, use a k×k grid and enlarge squares in the leftover row/column by shrinking the complementary ones. This packs n = k² + r squares better than pure gri

Add a continuous local optimizer: after building the best grid-based candidate, run a few hundred iterations of random perturbation + greedy acceptance on all square parameters (position, angle, side) with an exact overlap check to squeeze out extra area lost to the rigid grid layout.

Replace the heuristic candidate testing with an exact analytical solution of the piecewise-linear 1D optimization for each (a,b) grid-plus-partial-row layout, considering both the case where the partial-row squares are width-limited and where they are height-limited, and also try the complementary o

Add a scipy-based nonlinear local optimizer (SLSQP) that, starting from the best grid candidate, perturbs centres slightly and re-optimizes all square sizes jointly, using pairwise separation constraints for axis-aligned squares. This targets the small-n cases where grid layouts leave visible slack
